newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI SAYS NO PLANS TO MEET ZAIRE REBELS.
newsitem.headline: JCI SAYS NO PLANS TO MEET ZAIRE REBELS.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd said on Tuesday it had sent a team to Zaire to look at the management of some of its small engineering projects, but stressed it had no plans to meet Laurent Kabila's rebels.

JCI spokesman Marc Gonsalves said the company has been active in Zaire for some time, mainly through its projects division which held contracts with state-owned Gecamines (Generale des Carriers et des Mines) for small engineering projects.

"A small team from JCI projects is currently on a routine business trip to Zaire to look at the management of these operations. The team has no plans to meet with any political representatives during its visit," Gonsalves said.
JCI was one of the companies which submitted bids for the Kolwezi copper/cobalt tailings project and the open pit copper/cobatl mine at Ruashi-Etoile near Zaire's copper capital Lumbumbashi.

Kabila's rebels announced last week that U.S.-based America Mineral Fields Inc (AMF) had been awarded the Kolwezi project, but President Mobutu Sese Seko's government said last Thursday it had annulled all contracts AMF held with Gecamines.
South Africa's Anglo American Corp , Gencor Ltd and Iscor Ltd all submitted bids for the Kolwezi project.

Anglo said on Monday some of its senior officials and others from De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd were on their third visit to Zaire in less than a month to talk with Zaire's rebels, battling to oust the ailing Mobutu.
An agreement between AMF and Anglo to jointly develop the Kolwezi project, was cancelled earlier this year.
De Beers held a contract with Mobutu's government to buy the production of state diamond company Societe Miniere de Bakwanga (MIBA) and also maintained five diamond buying offices throughout Zaire.

De Beers -- which controls the world diamond trade through the London-based Central Selling Organisation -- pulled staff out of Kisangani in December and from the diamond capital Mbuji-Mayi a few weeks ago.
